briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 1, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Urgent Warnings
sections.content: Today's news once again highlights the severity of the global climate crisis. Pacific islanders are facing ruin due to climate change, and in Africa, farmers are frustrated by extreme weather, while rainmakers are confronting violence [29, 37]. A UN report identifies the United States as a major cause of the global retreat in climate change response, raising concerns that some US states are experiencing the steepest temperature increases due to global warming [33, 34]. Amidst the growing recognition that individual nations' goodwill alone cannot avert the climate crisis [1], a strong warning, 'Climate change is killing us,' has been issued ahead of COP31, and African negotiators have begun their COP31 strategy meeting amidst urgent El Niño warnings, emphasizing the urgency of global cooperation [35, 38].

sections.title: 🇰🇷🌱 Diverse Efforts and Technological Innovation for Carbon Neutrality in Korea
sections.content: In Korea, various efforts and technological innovations are actively underway to achieve carbon neutrality. KAIST Graduate School of Green Growth and Newton have initiated joint research on AI-based climate change response, emphasizing the role of science and technology [2]. Daejeon City is discussing ways to simultaneously pursue carbon neutrality and local industrial growth using climate tech [4, 6, 13], and the Chungnam Credit Guarantee Foundation has launched the 'Chungnam Public Institution Carbon Neutrality Working Group,' the first of its kind in the province, to encourage carbon neutrality practices in the public sector [7, 12, 20]. Particularly in the Incheon area, led by the Incheon Institute, efforts are accelerating to establish citizen-led carbon neutrality practices, including expanding citizen participation and concretizing 9 community-based carbon neutrality initiatives [8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 18]. The Asan City Council's Special Committee on Carbon Neutrality is also strengthening the carbon neutrality capabilities of the local community by conducting capacity-building training for its members [17].

sections.title: 🌱⚠️ Progress and Challenges in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is showing significant progress both domestically and internationally. As the Australian renewable energy market opens, K-green companies are entering the market with hydrogen and AI technologies [21], and in Damyang, a regulatory innovation MOU for establishing an RE100 industrial ecosystem to expand renewable energy supply has been signed [24]. In Seoul, the renewable energy production from buildings reviewed over the past five years has shown a significant increase, reaching 1.5 times the annual power generation of the Seoul Thermal Power Plant [25]. However, conflicts also exist in the policy implementation process, such as demands for the immediate withdrawal of the Korea Rural Community Corporation's designation as a renewable energy supplier [22]. Meanwhile, farmers whose livelihoods are threatened by climate change are filing 'climate lawsuits' against Korea Electric Power Corporation and public power generation companies, receiving public support [27], further highlighting issues of social responsibility related to energy transition.

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Diplomacy and the Importance of Responsibility
sections.content: The international community is focusing on diplomatic efforts and corporate responsibility in response to climate change. Brazilian President Lula is scheduled to attend the COP31 Climate Summit in Türkiye [36], and African negotiators are engaging in global negotiations, having commenced their COP31 strategy meeting amidst urgent El Niño warnings [38]. Discussions are active regarding the essential role of corporate responsibility in climate change [32], and the importance of environmental justice is also being emphasized [31]. According to interesting scientific research, there is a suggestion that we would currently be entering an ice age if not for climate change [28], and expectations are growing regarding AI's potential to offer innovative solutions to combat climate change [30].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the urgency of the climate crisis, as well as the diverse efforts and challenges, both domestic and international, to address it. International cooperation and responsible action are more critical than ever for a sustainable future. This concludes the climate briefing for November 1, 2026.

Citizens have sent letters to the court to support the 'climate lawsuit' filed by farmers, who feel their livelihoods threatened by climate change, against Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and public power generation companies. There is a broad consensus that this lawsuit extends beyond compensation for agricultural damage, touching upon the future of citizens facing the climate crisis.

summary.outlook: This lawsuit extends beyond agricultural damage compensation, connecting to the future of citizens facing the climate crisis. It is expected to spark broader societal discussions on climate crisis response and accountability.
